description: Mole Negro is the crown jewel of Oaxacan cuisine, a rich and deeply complex sauce that balances sweet, savory, and spicy notes. This traditional black mole features an array of chilies, spices, nuts, seeds, and a hint of chocolate, simmered to perfection. It is a labor of love that rewards with an unforgettable culinary experience, often served with tender chicken or turkey.

ingredients.notes: dried, stems and seeds removed (if available)

instructions.title: Prepare and Rehydrate Chilies
instructions.text: Toast the dried chilies lightly on a dry comal or skillet until fragrant, about 30 seconds per side. Be careful not to burn them. Transfer the toasted chilies to a bowl, cover with hot water, and let them rehydrate for 20-30 minutes until soft. Drain the chilies, reserving some of the soaking liquid.

instructions.title: Roast Aromatics and Spices
instructions.text: In a separate pan, dry roast the tomatoes, tomatillos, onion, and garlic until softened and slightly charred. Separately, toast the almonds, peanuts, sesame seeds, pumpkin seeds, cinnamon stick, cloves, peppercorns, cumin seeds, and anise seeds until fragrant. Keep an eye on the sesame seeds as they burn quickly.

instructions.title: Fry Remaining Ingredients
instructions.text: Heat a little lard or oil in a skillet. Fry the tortillas, bread, raisins, and optional plantain slices until golden. Remove and set aside. Ensure all ingredients are prepared for blending.

instructions.title: Blend the Mole Paste
instructions.text: Combine the rehydrated chilies, roasted vegetables, toasted nuts and seeds, fried tortillas, bread, raisins, plantain (if used), and a cup of chicken broth in a blender. Blend until a very smooth paste forms, adding more chicken broth or reserved chili soaking liquid as needed to achieve a thick, pourable consistency. Strain the paste through a fine-mesh sieve into a bowl to remove any solids, pressing with a spoon.

instructions.title: Cook the Mole Base
instructions.text: Heat the 1/4 cup of lard or oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Carefully pour the strained mole paste into the hot fat. It will sputter, so be cautious. Cook the paste, stirring constantly, for at least 15-20 minutes, or until it darkens significantly and thickens, reducing its volume. This step is crucial for flavor development.

instructions.title: Simmer and Season the Mole
instructions.text: Gradually stir in the remaining hot chicken broth, a cup at a time, until the mole reaches your desired consistency. Add the chopped Mexican chocolate and piloncillo (or brown sugar). Continue to simmer for at least 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, allowing the flavors to meld and the chocolate to fully dissolve. Season with salt to taste. The mole should be rich, dark, and slightly thick.

instructions.title: Serve with Chicken
instructions.text: Add the cooked chicken pieces to the simmering mole and cook for another 10-15 minutes, allowing them to absorb the rich flavors. Serve the Mole Negro hot, garnished with a sprinkle of sesame seeds and a side of white rice or warm tortillas. Enjoy this Oaxacan masterpiece!

tips: Toasting the chilies and spices properly is essential; it deepens their flavor. Be careful not to burn them, as this will make the mole bitter.
Straining the mole paste is a traditional step that ensures a silky smooth texture. Dont skip it for the best results.
Mole freezes beautifully. Make a large batch and store portions for up to 3 months. Reheat gently, adding a little broth if needed.
article:
Unlock the secrets of one of Mexico's most revered culinary treasures: Mole Negro Oaxacan Black Mole. This isn't just a sauce; it's a symphony of flavors, a historical narrative, and a testament to the rich gastronomic heritage of Oaxaca, Mexico. Often considered the queen of moles, its deep, complex taste and iconic dark hue make it a showstopper at any dinner table. While its preparation is a labor of love, the reward is an unparalleled culinary experience that transports you straight to the heart of Mexico. If you're ready to embark on a journey of discovery and delight your senses with an authentic Mexican dinner recipe, then delving into the world of Mole Negro is an absolute must.

## What is Mole Negro Oaxacan Black Mole?

Mole Negro, meaning "black mole," is the most famous and intricate of Oaxaca's "seven moles." Hailing from the southwestern state of Oaxaca, often called "The Land of Seven Moles," this particular mole stands out for its profound dark color and extraordinarily complex flavor profile. It's not merely dark chocolate that gives it its signature shade, but a meticulous combination of charred chiles, toasted nuts, seeds, spices, fruits, and a touch of Mexican chocolate, all ground into a velvety, rich sauce.

The Oaxacan Black Mole is renowned for its harmonious balance of smoky, sweet, spicy, and earthy notes. It's a dish steeped in tradition, often reserved for significant celebrations such as weddings, quinceañeras, Day of the Dead, and other major fiestas. Each family often has its own cherished recipe, passed down through generations, making every Mole Negro a unique expression of culinary heritage. The depth of flavor comes from a slow, patient cooking process, allowing dozens of ingredients to meld into a sauce that is truly greater than the sum of its parts.

## Ingredients You Need

Preparing an authentic Mole Negro Oaxacan Black Mole requires a pantry full of diverse ingredients. Don't be intimidated by the list; each component plays a vital role in building the layered flavors.

*   **Dried Chiles:** The backbone of Mole Negro. You'll need a combination of Mulato, Pasilla Oaxaca, Ancho, and sometimes a smoky Chipotle or two. These provide depth, heat, and that characteristic dark color.
*   **Aromatics:** White onion, garlic, ripe tomatoes, and tomatillos.
*   **Nuts & Seeds:** Almonds, peanuts, sesame seeds, pepitas (pumpkin seeds), and sometimes pecans. These add richness and help thicken the sauce.
*   **Spices:** Cumin seeds, coriander seeds, whole cloves, cinnamon stick (Mexican canela is best), black peppercorns, dried oregano (Mexican oregano preferred), and thyme.
*   **Sweeteners/Fats/Flavor Enhancers:** Mexican chocolate (unsweetened or very dark, about 70-80% cacao), plantain (ripe, almost black), raisins, lard or vegetable oil.
*   **Thickeners:** A few stale corn tortillas or a slice of day-old bread.
*   **Liquid:** Rich chicken broth (homemade is ideal).
*   **Seasoning:** Salt to taste.

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Making Oaxacan Black Mole is a journey, not a sprint. Allocate a good portion of your day, or even two, for this rewarding endeavor.

1.  **Prepare the Chiles:** Carefully remove stems and seeds from all dried chiles. Open them flat. Heat a dry comal or skillet over medium heat and toast the chiles in batches for about 30 seconds per side until fragrant but not burnt (burning will make them bitter). Immediately transfer them to a bowl, cover with very hot water, and let them rehydrate for 20-30 minutes until soft.
2.  **Toast Nuts, Seeds & Spices:** In a clean, dry skillet, toast the sesame seeds until golden. Remove. Then, toast the almonds, peanuts, and pepitas separately until fragrant. Set aside. Next, lightly toast the cumin, coriander, cloves, cinnamon, and peppercorns until aromatic.
3.  **Fry Aromatics & Thickeners:** Heat a generous amount of lard or oil in a large pot or Dutch oven. Fry the chopped onion and garlic until softened. Add the tomatoes, tomatillos, and the sliced plantain, frying until slightly caramelized. In the same oil, quickly fry the tortilla pieces or bread until lightly golden.
4.  **Blend Everything:** Drain the rehydrated chiles, reserving some of the soaking liquid. In a high-speed blender, combine the softened chiles, fried aromatics, plantain, raisins, toasted nuts, seeds, and spices. Add the Mexican chocolate and about 2 cups of chicken broth. Blend until incredibly smooth. This may require several batches and possibly straining the mixture through a fine-mesh sieve for the smoothest texture (this step is optional but highly recommended for a truly refined mole).
5.  **Cook the Mole:** Heat a fresh amount of lard or oil in your large pot over medium heat. Carefully pour the blended mole paste into the hot oil. This step is crucial; it "fries" the mole, deepening its flavor and ensuring proper emulsification. Stir constantly to prevent sticking and burning. The mole will thicken and darken, and the oil will separate slightly. This process can take 15-20 minutes.
6.  **Simmer and Season:** Once the mole has fried, gradually add the remaining chicken broth, stirring continuously. Bring it to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover partially, and let it cook for at least 1-2 hours, stirring frequently to prevent sticking. The longer it simmers, the more the flavors will meld and deepen. Add salt to taste throughout the simmering process. The finished Oaxacan Black Mole should be thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

Crafting the perfect Oaxacan Black Mole is an art form, and these tips will help you achieve a truly spectacular result:

*   **Quality Chiles are Key:** Seek out fresh, pliable dried chiles from a reputable Mexican market. Their aroma and freshness significantly impact the final flavor.
*   **Don't Burn the Chiles:** When toasting chiles, a slight char is good for smokiness, but burning makes them bitter. Keep a close eye and work quickly.
*   **Blend Until Silky Smooth:** A smooth mole is a hallmark of authenticity. If your blender isn't super powerful, strain the mole through a fine-mesh sieve after blending. This removes any fibrous bits from the chiles and ensures a luxurious texture.
*   **The "Frying" Step is Non-Negotiable:** Sautéing the blended mole paste in hot lard or oil is essential for developing its deep, complex flavors. Don't rush this step.
*   **Patience, Patience, Patience:** Mole is a slow food. The long, gentle simmer allows all the disparate flavors to meld into a cohesive, rich sauce. Taste and adjust seasoning as it cooks.
*   **Make it Ahead:** Mole improves significantly after a day or two, allowing the flavors to deepen and harmonize even further. It also freezes beautifully.

## Serving Suggestions

Traditionally, Mole Negro Oaxacan Black Mole is served with tender pieces of cooked chicken or turkey. The rich, savory sauce perfectly complements the mild poultry.

*   **Classic Pairing:** Ladle generously over braised chicken thighs or breasts.
*   **Accompaniments:** Serve with fluffy white rice, warm corn tortillas for scooping, and perhaps a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds or fresh cilantro for garnish.
*   **Beyond Poultry:** Don't limit yourself! Mole Negro is also fantastic with roasted pork loin, duck, or even as a unique sauce for tamales or enchiladas. For a vegetarian option, try it with roasted sweet potatoes, plantains, or hearty mushrooms.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the traditional recipe for Oaxacan Black Mole is specific, minor adjustments can be made based on availability or dietary needs.

*   **Chiles:** If Pasilla Oaxaca is difficult to find, you can substitute with more Pasilla Negro or even a combination of Ancho and a smoky Morita chile for similar depth.
*   **Nuts/Seeds:** Feel free to adjust the ratio of nuts and seeds, or omit one if there's an allergy, understanding that the flavor profile will subtly shift.
*   **Chocolate:** If Mexican chocolate is unavailable, use a high-quality unsweetened or very dark (75%+) chocolate, adding a pinch of cinnamon and a tiny amount of piloncillo or brown sugar if needed to balance the bitterness.
*   **Vegetarian:** For a plant-based version, use vegetable broth instead of chicken broth and serve over roasted vegetables, seitan, or hearty legumes.

Embrace the culinary adventure of making Mole Negro. This iconic Mexican dinner recipe is more than just food; it's a celebration of culture, history, and the incredible art of flavor. While the ingredient list and steps may seem daunting, the process itself is meditative, and the resulting Oaxacan Black Mole is a masterpiece that will undoubtedly impress and delight. So, gather your ingredients, clear your schedule, and prepare to create a truly unforgettable meal.
